Hot Wheels RC Car, Remote-Control 2017 Nissan GT-R in 1:64 Scale, Works On and Off Hot Wheels Track, Includes Track Adapter​​​​ I got two of these Hot Wheels remote control cars - the Hot Wheels R/C 1:64 Scale 2017 Nissan Gt-R and the Rodger Dodger. First off, I have to say that they are lots of fun.

They run on the floor well, but they also fit our Hot Wheels track, giving a variety of interesting options - but I preferred the floor as you have freeform options you won't have on the track. As an example, if you want to turn around dramatically, just turn with the remote without going forward or back. But they're a blast when you run one on the track, as well! They're faster than I thought they'd be, and while it took a few minutes to get used to the steering on the remote, after that they were responsive and easy to control. I let my husband drive the Gt-R so we could race, and he also had a learning curve with the steering and then found the car to be a blast.

I like the way the remotes bind without a hassle, and you can control either car with either remote, but it won't control both simultaneously, so no problem for racing.

I really like these cars, although I think the 2017 Nissan Gt-R is more attractive, but that's a personal taste thing. Both cars are fun, run well, and you can do a few tricks with them. They run well on our hardwood floors and can be raced using Hot Wheels track, as well. I think one of these cars would make a good gift for older kids as well as anyone into Hot Wheels.

It would be nice if a timer was on this thing because it would totally be the responsibility of the "baker" to hear the timer go off, then go get the item and let it cool. Hasbro Gaming Battleship Shots We've only had this a few days so far, but my kids love it so far! They and their neighborhood friends were playing almost non-stop this entire weekend. It's a pretty unique concept and not at all what I expected coming from the original battleship: Rather than the game of strategy (and sometimes just luck!) that the traditional battleship is, this is mostly a game of skill. There is still some strategy in how you align your boats, but rather than try to determine where the other player's position is, you can see their board and have to toss one of the included ping-pong balls into the holes. Land a ball in all the boat's places, and you've sunk their ship! It is definitely reminiscent of beer pong in skillset, or perhaps one of those arcade games that require you to land a ball in a colored cup. You definitely need more space to play since there will be balls bouncing around if/when you miss, but it is a lot of fun. A creative twist on a classic game!
One thing that is a little strange to me however, is the advertising. The listing for this product says "Nostalgic tabletop gameplay meets interactive digital content for an immersive gaming experience". There's nothing digital about this, let alone interactive digital and immersive. It's a pretty fun analog pick-up-and-play game, which is what I like about it actually, but it was hard to determine what we were getting before we tried it.
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Gaming Battleship Shots

The caveats are that you have the ability to "play it safe", which can avoid getting out if someone accuses you of trying to steal on your turn. This can lead to many rounds where nothing happens as someone needs to steal or accuse of stealing for the game to progress. It is also possible to start feeling repetitive after some time as the gameplay does not allow for much variation to keep it interesting. For what it is, it is a fun quick game that doesn't require a lot of setup or learning. But don't expect it to last a long time before people want to do something else instead.
text_fidelity_b: Playin' Possum

text_fidelity_a:
dreambuilderToy Building Bricks 1100 Pieces Set with All Popular Building Blocks The theme for my five-year old's birthday party was Lego Batman. Therefore, I needed a bunch of Lego bricks to make decorations, but I did not want to pay an expensive Lego price and I also just needed basic bricks and colors. Enter the Dreambuilder Toy Building Bricks with 1000 bricks! Not only did I get exactly what I wanted, but I also got a superior toy. I was able to "build" all the decorations I needed (a napkin and silverware holder) with lots of bricks to spare, but when the party was over, I gave my son all the bricks and he was none the wiser that these were not "real" Legos. Some of the older boys at the party inspected the decorations and were able to come to a conclusion that these were in fact not real Legos, but that does not matter because they function exactly like real Legos.

Within the bag you get basic bricks in various sizes, 1x1, 2x2, 2x6, 2x8, etc. There is also one small, green building plate. The set also comes with various bricks for roofs, doors, fences, and windows. The colors are Roy G. Biv with black, white, and grey added. There are equal amounts of each color. We do have a real Lego 1000 piece "creative" bucket and here are the differences. There is no idea booklet with this. However, I do believe you can check their website for building ideas. Therefore, if free form building is not for your child like it is for mine, then this set is not for you. There is no brick separator, and the really flat bricks that drove us adults insane when we were kids are back to haunt to us. You will need to purchase one separately unlike the Lego creative sets. The Lego creative sets have more unique bricks, which take away from having more basic bricks to build bigger and better things as you would with this set. Dreambuilder bricks do not come with a storage bucket. You will receive a plastic bag with all of the bricks contained within that bag. So, you will need your own storage box.

Overall, I find the Dreambuilder bricks to be vastly superior to Lego if you are into simple, old school, free building without instructions. I will be purchasing additional sets.
text_fidelity_b: dreambuilderToy Building Bricks 1100 Pieces Set with All Popular Building Blocks

text_fidelity_a:
Bop It XT Finding a children's toy that can actually entertain....especially during a time (in our country) where kids spend most of there time on the IPod Touch, Xbox, WII, PSP, computers etc. is difficult. We live in a society of computer generated video games, computer enhanced movies, 3D, 4D, special effects, etc, and I find myself asking my kids -what happened to Connect 4, Twister, Simon, UNO, Clue, Life, Scrabble, PAC Man and Monopoly? Basically my childhood was filled with memories of playing these kinds of games, meaning those that essentially force you to interact with people. Under this belief, seeing the "Bop It " I thought maybe ...just maybe my kids (10 & 13) would enjoy playing this on family night. Believe it or not, while it is not animated and gloomy, it gave us hours of pure, clean fun. We battled each other. We laughed and teased. While the game kind of reminded me of Simon, it was surprisingly a bit more complicated. For Simon you just have to remember the color sequences, while the Bop challenges you to complete several tasks.....to pull, twist, flick, roll... quickly or you're out. The minute you miss, you have to start again. There is also a commentator giving the score, and teasing the player. My 13-year-old thought that this would be fun game to take on road trips (to play between all of his other electronics), while my 10-year-old is more determined than ever to beat his present score. Both found "Bop It" to be an easy to understand/fun game that promotes coordination and interacting with others. I highly recommend it.

It's light-weight and easy to carry.
It's stylish. Looks a little Jazzy...each task is a different color and shape.
It would definitely teach kids to listen. Following directions is a crucial element for playing the game.
text_fidelity_b: Bop It XT

Ontel Magic Tracks The Amazing Racetrack That Can Bend, Flex and Glow - As Seen On TV Multicolor, 11' Like many people, I have seen this product advertised on television and was excited to see if it is as fun as it looks in the commercials. The set comes with 1 car, a sheet of stickers to decorate the car, and 20 track segments in four different colors. The car requires 2 AAA batteries that are NOT included. The track segments are made of small individual pieces, which is why the box says it comes with 220 pieces of track.

The track is flexible and can be arranged in many different ways, and each segment can be used as a straight or curved part of the track. The car worked well and stayed on the track. A small pamphlet with quick trips is included with ideas on making the track more fun. I used the cardboard pieces used to package the car to create a small ramp and tunnel which worked better than I expected. After the track pieces were exposed to bright light, they did slightly glow in the dark. However, the box shows a picture of a looped track. I tried both a couple types of loops and none of them worked because the flexible track wouldn't support the weight of the car. In spite of this, this is a fun racetrack set that allows for a lot of different track formations to keep kids interested.
text_fidelity_b: Ontel Magic Tracks The Amazing Racetrack That Can Bend, Flex and Glow - As Seen On TV Multicolor, 11'

That said, these kits are made for kids eight and up but honeslty, I think they should be marketed for any person 8 and up, since adults may like to try some of these crafts too. text_fidelity_a: 4M T-Rex Dinosaur DNA Kit, 4945, Multi What kid doesn't like dinosaurs?  This is perfert for your boy or girl who is into dinosaurs.  I suppose it could be considered an educational toy, but probably only marginally so.  Who says educational toys can't be fun too?  This is especially nice for a kid interested in archeology.  Contains a block of plaster that has embedded into it "DNA" stickers and a glow in the dark dinosaur.  After the fun of digging out the dinosaur and stickers with the included digging tools and brush, they are left with a dinosaur model, so even though the digging fun is over after one time (if they do it all at once), there is something to show for it.  There are also two "augmented reality" (AR) play mats that are completed with the DNA stickers that have been "excavated".  The mats when used with a cell phone and an application from the App Store (for Apple phones) or the Google Play Store (for Androids) produces a 3D dinosaur, visible on the phone.  One problem with this is that it might not work with all cell phones.  It is supposed to work with MOST Apple devices (8.0 and above).  On Android phones the only devices tested are Google Nexus Series, Samsung Galaxy S5 and Samsung Galaxy Tab.  I didn't have a cell phone to test this on, but it seems like it still might be fun even if that part doesn't work.  It's just that you might not be able to use the full capability of the kit if your phone doesn't work with the application.  Also if you give this to a child of only 8 (the lower age limit on this), they may not yet have a cell and you may not want them to have one at that age.  Since this contains many small parts, it needs to be kept away from small children, as there is a choking hazard (box says no one under 3).  I would have loved a toy like this when I was a kid.  Just remember to put down a newspaper when they are working on the plaster block in order to collect all the plaster pieces that are chipped off as they excavate.  Pricing of the kit is very reasonable.  Made in China.
text_fidelity_b: 4M T-Rex Dinosaur DNA Kit, 4945, Multi

text_fidelity_a: Disney Colorbrain, The Ultimate Board Game for Families who Love Disney This game is harder than you might think. I thought my Disney knowledge was pretty good, but I was stumped on maybe 1/3 of the questions during the two games I played. My younger Disneyphiles did about the same as me. You might remember that the caterpillar in Alice in Wonderland is blue, but can you recall the color of the flags that sit atop the hats of the Tweedles? There are some questions that require you to come up with as many as five different colors, all of which must be correct for you to gain a point. What color is Celia's dress from Monsters Inc? What three colors are seen in Go Go Tomago's superhero suit from Big Hero 6?  You need to answer quickly, by putting down your selected color cards in front of you. This is actually pretty fun and interesting. Minor characters can be especially tricky. There were a few cards with answers that we disagreed with, such as the one that said Joy from Inside Out wore a yellow dress, when we all see it as green. The answer cards all have pictures from the animated films, and sometimes the photo is not great quality. My family enjoyed this game despite these issues and found it a more challenging activity than we had anticipated. It takes almost no time to learn how to set up and play. You can fill ten minutes or half an hour easily.
text_fidelity_b: Disney Colorbrain, The Ultimate Board Game for Families who Love Disney

PAI TECHNOLOGY Botzees Easy-to-Build 6-in-1 Coding Robots for Kids with Puzzles, Augmented Reality STEM Toy, Ages 4,5,6,7,8,9,10+ Year Old Boys and Girls (App Based) I gave this PAI TECHNOLOGY Botzees Building and Coding - Construction Kit with Puzzles, Augmented Reality to my 7 year old son as a gift from Santa. In comparison to other robot building kits, I wasn't that impressed. First of all, you MUST have an updated iOs or Android phone/tablet. I am unsure if Android has this problem, but if you have an iPhone 5 or 6 and you can't update to the latest iOs, you will not be able to use this robot. Also, since this is an augmented reality app, I doubt that the Kindle Fire will work on this. The camera just isn't powerful enough. I ran into this problem with my son's Fire HD 10 for other AR programs. Next, when you unbox, there are no instructions. You have to go a website to get the instruction manual, which could have been printed on the two cards in the box that say go to the website for a manual. Finally, this does not come with a power source. There is a lithium battery and a USB cable, but you will have to have your own plug. Obviously, many of us will already have various plugs, but to have a designated plug would be nice considering the amount asked for this product.

Overall, my son's interest in this was limited. He's much more interested using his other building toys and finding ways for them to move. I think he feels limited in his creativity. You cannot use this without the App, so any ideas he has of incorporating other mediums to this has him frustrated. It's a nice idea. However, considering that I try to limit his screen time as well it would be nice to have an off screen option to play with this.
text_fidelity_b: PAI TECHNOLOGY Botzees Easy-to-Build 6-in-1 Coding Robots for Kids with Puzzles, Augmented Reality STEM Toy, Ages 4,5,6,7,8,9,10+ Year Old Boys and Girls (App Based)

Her skirt is a cute, candy print fabric, but the material itself is stiff and doesn't flow or move. In fact, I don't like the skirt at all. text_fidelity_a:
Green Toys Farm Playset - 13 Piece Pretend Play, Motor Skills, Language & Communication Kids Role Play Toy. No BPA, phthalates, PVC. Dishwasher Safe, Recycled Plastic, Made in USA, Red, Pack of 1 I really like that green toys uses recycled plastic and makes a variety of very simple, imagination based toys that are fun for kids to play with. This toy really seems to have a lot of potential in that regard. There are large barn doors on both sides of the barn that open and shut, and it open and airy second level where the sheep and pigs can hang out and look out the window, etc.

The fencing and the little covered area presumably for a trough are getting ignored at our house, I have a three-year-old and a not quite one-year-old, but the barn itself, simple animals, and truck were greeted with boos and eyes upon opening, and have been in play ever since, not only with the things that came in the set but with their other toys, which is really what one hopes when buying an open-ended toy like this. The truck has enough room to put action figures, Lego bricks, pig, etc. in there, and the barn is the same.

I have one quibble, actually two: while the barn seems like it should fit the truck, when you try to close the doors, the truck squirts out the back doors. When you go to close the back doors, it squirts out the front doors. There's not enough room in the barn to park the truck, even though (and this is what my problem with it is) it looks like it was meant to be parked in there. My toddler can be a little bit uptight about these types of things and when he is in a bad mood, this failure of the truck to park properly in the barn really upsets him. How hard would it have been to design these figures so that they all worked gracefully together? I think many toddlers would have really appreciated that thoughtful touch.

My other minor quibble is that the cow figures stand on two legs and are dressed as farmers. We try to present things that are at least a little bit based in reality to our children of this age, and so a cow dressed as a farmer would not have been my first choice. I would've preferred one farmer and one cow that actually looked like a cow, or two cows and no farmer, if they were worried about what color of plastic to make a farmer so that it appealed to everybody. I think they wanted a farmer figure to sit in the truck and drive it, and that is nice but not 100% necessary.

Overall, this is an awesome set and would make a fabulous gift for families that have kids of different ages. I personally am getting rid of the fencing and covered outdoor red thing, plus the weird cow farmers, but the base set – a barn, some pigs and sheep, and the truck, are awesome. Even though you would give the gift perhaps to one child, it is nice that everybody can play with it, it is not gender-based, and it has potential to be played with in a variety of ways as the child or children grow. Another win for green toys!
text_fidelity_b: Green Toys Farm Playset - 13 Piece Pretend Play, Motor Skills, Language & Communication Kids Role Play Toy. No BPA, phthalates, PVC. Dishwasher Safe, Recycled Plastic, Made in USA, Red, Pack of 1

text_fidelity_a:
SKLZ Pro Mini Basketball Hoop A simple way to amuse and practice your shot, the SKLZ Pro Mini Basketball Hoop offers glow in the dark appeal, easy assembly, and hours of fun. It hooks on the top of most doors so you can lie in bed and practice shooting or attach it to your office door at work for some quick stress relief.

Out of the box, this basketball hoop requires some assembly, but it shouldn’t take long to attach the parts and prep it for use. The hooks that attach it to a door are not adjustable, but they are designed to fit a wide range of door thicknesses. After attaching, you may notice that it lacks stability. I noticed it, too, but I also found that it didn’t matter. It doesn’t need to be completely stable because the weight of the included basketball is so light. Throw after throw results in no bouncing or other movement for me, so don’t worry if the hoop seems less secure than you would prefer. Unless your door is very thin, it should be fine.

Once you have the ball inflated, the toy is ready for use. You may want to set everything in direct light for a few hours at first, to help with the glowing. If you don’t, then the glow will be very faint. Still, it should be enough to make it visible in the dark so that, if you use this at home, you or your kids can see it in the dark and play before you fall asleep. One thing that new buyers need to realize is that, due to the thickness of the hooks, it may not be possible to close the door to which this is attached. My door won’t close, but I attached it to a door that normally stays open all of the time anyway. If your door won’t close with this attached, then you will have no choice but to go back and forth, taking it down and putting it back up.

Overall, this seems like a good toy and it should be fun for the basketball enthusiast in your home. There is no glass and the construction is made to last. The glow in the dark feature could be better, but other than that, it seems like an entertaining way to pass the time.
text_fidelity_b: SKLZ Pro Mini Basketball Hoop

Bobby Fischer® Learn to Play Chess Set Board Game, Easy to Understand - How to Play Chess Book, 34 Plastic Staunton Chess Pieces, Folding Illustrated Chess Board, Family Games for Kids and Adults When I was in middle school, a teacher I did not really know invited me in to learn chess. It changed my life. I wanted to pass the information on to my kids, but it was hard to get them to make connections. This set is great.

WHAT IS THIS SET LIKE?
This set comes with a four fold board, big sized pieces, general instructions, and two dice.

BOARD
The board has information right on it, so that you don't have to repeat it over and over for visual learners.

PIECES
The pieces in this box are plenty big enough, have a nice felt bottom and are all in the box. Nothing was missing. There were even the two extra queens in the box too.

IS IT EASY TO TEACH WITH?
I found that this is really easy to teach with and in my case, it has been a while since I could play chess with someone and not a computer, so I found this very exciting.

DICE
The dice is a great way to even out playing with a beginner which helps a lot because who wants to be beaten constantly?

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a great set for a beginner chess learner. The board is small, the pieces easy to use and the directions clear and well laid out. The dice make it fun for mis matched players (beginner vs more advanced).

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I like this set and am glad to have it. My family is finally going to learn chess without me having to continually explain everything. The visuals are great.
text_fidelity_b: Bobby Fischer® Learn to Play Chess Set Board Game, Easy to Understand - How to Play Chess Book, 34 Plastic Staunton Chess Pieces, Folding Illustrated Chess Board, Family Games for Kids and Adults

LEGO Classic Bricks and Houses 11008 Kids’ Building Toy Starter Set with Fun Builds to Stimulate Young Minds (270 Pieces) The Lego Classic Bricks and Houses set is more open ended than themed sets. The included instructions give steps for a small house, a castle, an igloo, a windmill, a family home, and a lighthouse. You can build all of these at the same time, without having to deconstruct anything.

This set reminded me of when I was a kid, taking out my bucket of Legos and just building whatever came to mind, instead of following the instructions to a specific set.

This set includes a good assortment of colors and pieces, and hopefully the different building techniques and different house styles will inspire kids to try out their own house, or whatever else they want to build. That’s the aim of the Lego Classic line, to inspire kids to make their own creations, and I think the pieces here are good for that.

It could make a good gift for the beginning Lego builder, especially if you’re unsure of what theme they might prefer, or be a good complement to other Lego Classic sets.

Educational Insights Artie 3000 the Coding & Drawing Robot, STEM Toy, Gift for Boys & Girls, Ages 7+ The instructions in the box are lacking and the website is only slightly better. There isn't anything to download to get it to work. It works, the few times it works, via a web browser.

The device itself has a built in WiFi connection. You can, I think, secure it with a password if you want. It's open by default. You connect to it as a WiFi connection then go to its website to get it to work. I find it hangs nearly constantly. Out of the first ten tries, it worked once, each time running the same code. Here I will point out, I can't get it to go and I'm a senior software developer.

It runs on a very small surface. A sheet of 8 1/2 x 11 printer paper is perfect. It has no edge detection, so mind it doesn't wander off the edge of the table. It starts with the pen fully down by necessity, or at least I can't get it to do anything unless I fully seat the pen, which means it will touch the paper when it is set down,, so it will leave a blob that will bleed through the average paper. Indeed, these bleed almost as bad an an alcohol-based marker.

While it will work with JavaScript or Python, it provides no insight into how to use these languages, so if your kid knows Python they can learn to code the robot in Python, which just means learning its custom library. I would not go so far as to say it teaches much of anything. Hour of code shows as much, is free, and is far more reliable.

It's cute, but until the bugs are worked out, it's not worth the hassle.

There's a certain thrill of putting in raw stones that you think are "pretty", only to see their true beauty one they are polished.

text_fidelity_a:
Franklin Sports Giant Wooden Dice These dice are beautifully made of solid pine. Playing games with these are fun but play responsibly. Displaying the dice as works of art is equally as great.

Provided in the package:
- Six die that weigh a combined 4.6 pounds. (See the attached pictures for an idea of size relative to two of my cats and their water fountain.)
- A strong canvas pouch for carrying the dice.
- A folded one-page pamphlet with two game variations and a sample score card for copying.

Each die is beautiful and each "number point" (i.e. dots) on the same die face is painted a rich coffee brown or dark tan. However, the "number points" are various shades of coffee brown on each side of the same die, so there is a slight inconsistency in color there. Nevertheless, this does not take away from their beauty. One should discount the "life-sized" claim. They are large but all of them stacked three high, side-by-side, do not even reach the height of a poised cat as you can see from my photos. When used for play instead of art, the round edge of each die provides for a smooth roll and reduction of injury to property or person. Although this is rated for ages 6 and above, I HIGHLY RECOMMEND children, adults, and pets stay far back when rolling the dice.

My boyfriend and I played the first game on my inside carpet since it was raining outside. I made sure to remove any items that could break around the area we were playing and I had to keep shooing the cats away. I originally thought we had to roll all six die at once (which is impossible). Therefore, when playing the two games in the instructions, roll each die one at a time because they are too large to roll together. The instructions should say that, however, because the first thought I had is "How am I going to roll these six die all at once," when the instructions said "roll the dice"?

My boyfriend loved the dice and the game even though I won. Since each die is heavy, it is extremely important to throw each die gently. I can see unsupervised children or drunk adults throwing these at each other and causing serious damage or death. As long as everyone plays responsibly, hours of fun and friendly competition are awaiting those who play this lawn or carpeted basement "game."
text_fidelity_b: Franklin Sports Giant Wooden Dice

text_fidelity_a:
Treasure X King's Gold Treasure Tomb We have had a few other Treasure X sets in the past and my son really enjoyed them, with the sets keeping him busy for hours at a time carving and opening little slime filled packages with interesting toys inside. He has a castle "dollhouse" that he uses a lot of these toys in to create stories.

This treasure tomb was completely different in the sense that we work carving the toys out of chunks of sand this time, rather discovering each element and kind of figuring out everything as a puzzle.

The one criticism I have is that while I would've loved to have set this down and let my son just figure it out, the texture of a few of the things that you were supposed to just pick apart and peel away were not necessarily obvious that they were disposable elements of the toy, so the instruction manual was necessary, and because the instruction manual was not made big and pictorial, I had to sit there while they figured the whole thing out. My six-year-old figured out and understood most of it, but again, the parts that were not obvious that he was allowed to just tear into them really did need my reading the instructions and giving encouragement.

Aside from that minor quibble, this thing kept both my six-year-old and my three and half-year-old busy for a really long time. Hours. I sat them outside on the patio with a big pan to hold any messy elements, and they carved and drove swords into holes and put the keys in and popped everything out and overall had a ridiculously fun time.

The weird textural blue rock like slime in two of the tombs was particularly compelling to my son, who played with this stuff for about 45 minutes. I would've appreciated if the two tombs had had different types of slime or even just different colors, but my son had no such complaint and played for a long time.

While the tomb itself has not continued to hold their interest after about a week of play, some of the parts have been incorporated into frequent play with their castle dollhouse, and so overall even though part of it feels somewhat disposable, the other parts of it feel really fun for incorporating into our normal imaginative play.

This would make a fantastic birthday gift, because it is extremely flashy, tons of fun, lots of excited commentary and wowed children, and then lots of little toys that feel very fun and abundant.

Would I buy a set like this again? Very possibly, for a holiday or other occasion that I really want to feel super special and fancy. If there was a holiday where we were unable to have family and friends visit us or something like that, this set would bridge the gap to make the day feel sparkly and exciting for the kids.
text_fidelity_b: Treasure X King's Gold Treasure Tomb

text_fidelity_a:
Mattel Barbie Hairtastic Color Stylin Doll As a longtime Barbie collector, I'm always curious when a new Barbie doll uses a gimmick that was popular years ago. In this case, the Barbie Hairtastic Color Styling doll offers the same "color magic" idea that made a 1966 Barbie doll a best-seller. The concept is similar - wet the doll's hair and you can change her hair color using a simple brush and a "foil clip".

This doll comes with a chair, water brush, comb, water bowl (for rinsing the brush), eight "foil" cards (purple, orange and pink), a set of three Barbie hairties, and a styling "foil clip".

The box makes the color transfer seem easy, but actually it takes a bit of work. The instructions say "wet the hair generously" so if you do this with a child, be sure to have a newspaper or towel around so that the doll's hair and the dyes don't stain your table. The foil clip comes already loaded with an orange card, so I tried that first.

The results were mixed. I had to run the clip up and down the hair a few times before the color started to show. I also had to reapply the wet brush several times even though the hair seemed wet enough. Finally, the orange color streak came out bright and strong. Then I tried the purple dye, and the color was faint and weak. I added more water and tried again, but the purple dye failed to transfer a rich color. Not sure why this is.

Contrary to the box claims, the foils can't be reused. It's low-tech - a swatch of watercolor paint on the back of a foil card. When some of the dye from the purple card failed to transfer, I simply took the card out of the clip and rubbed the card itself into the hair. This was sloppy but it did the job better.

The chair has a suction cup, which is a wonderful and long-needed feature. Barbie sat snugly in her chair and it remained firmly anchored while styling. I wish all Barbie chairs had something like this.

Lastly, the instructions don't mention how long the dye will last, only that it comes off with water. Good, but I found that the dye stained my hands and clothing. If a child does this, be prepared. The clip idea is good, but it doesn't fully prevent the process from getting messy.

Overall, it's a decent toy but once the dyes run out, you'd be left with an ordinary Barbie doll.
text_fidelity_b: Mattel Barbie Hairtastic Color Stylin Doll

text_fidelity_a:
Crayola Glow Book I never really thought I would be calling any toy a godsend, but the Crayola Glow Book has done something for my ten-year-old son that none of his school teachers (and certainly not his art teacher) has been able to do. I've tried, too. I've tried asking, showing, cajoling, ordering, limiting privileges, exaggerated sighing, and using his full name, but my child's penmanship is abysmal and his art skills mostly stink.

The reason for this is relatively straightforward: in my family, kids develop their fine motor skills later than most kids do. My parents and teachers made me work at it, but I at least was getting a lot of practice all the time. My child goes to a school where he gets to type a lot of his assignments. He's learned a lot in art about color and perspective and design, but he gets extremely frustrated trying to execute what's in his head, so he stopped enjoying drawing and painting pretty much as soon as he hit kindergarten.

When I ordered this, I thought it was going to turn out to be just a gimmicky gadgety thing he'd use once and then I'd get to use it to leave notes my husband would have to work to ignore, but my son loves it. He can write, draw, erase, illuminate, and animate without having to commit anything to paper or to critical eyes (except his own). Because the illustration plates are layered, if he's happy with one part but not another, he can re-do the one without having to worry about smudging or wrecking the other. As a result, he is spending time using his fine motor skills, they are improving, and he is much happier with the work he is doing.

I gave this five stars for fun, based on his recommendation. I rate it five stars for educational value and five stars overall for how much help it has been in an area in which my child needed some help. I gave it four stars for durability. It feels a little flimsy, but it's holding up well so far.

UPDATE: When you exhaust the markers that come with this, you can use dry erase markers on it. They're actually a little bit easier to see and work with, they come in tons of colors, and they clean right up.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Glow Book
